scale: Each factor is an integer from 1 (low) to 5 (high); score = (expected_impact*confidence*urgency)/(effort*risk), rounded to 4 places. Risk 1 is the lowest risk. tools/exposure_contracts.py recomputes every score and checks that ranks follow scores.
reading_note: The formula ranks quick, low-risk fixes first. It is an execution order, not a measure of upside: the Burlington page (rank 8) has the largest single on-site upside but more effort.
rescore_trigger: When baseline_metrics.json, competitor_intel.json and geo_grid_baseline.json hold collected data, and monthly after that.

levers.action: Confirm which repository and branch publish www.clearglassinc.com and make every site change there. This repository is not that source.
levers.rationale: Live sitemap (176 URLs) and homepage differ from this checkout (84 URLs after the 2026-11-21 prune); all 8 checkout-only sitemap URLs return 404 live; main's canonical-tag fixes, merged at 18:54 UTC on 2026-11-21, were still not live about four hours later. Site work here is wasted until the source is known. One clue: the live /procurement-legal-tech.html declares a canonical on clearglassinc.github.io.
levers.acceptance: The publishing repository is recorded in README.md and a test change in it appears on the live site.

levers.action: Decide whether ClearGlass meets clients in person during stated hours. If yes, create or claim a service-area Business Profile with the address hidden and the real-world name. If no, drop the geo-grid objective and compete in organic results only.
levers.rationale: Google: 'To qualify for a Business Profile, a business must make in-person contact with customers during its stated hours.' Online-only businesses are listed as ineligible. Without an eligible profile there is no local-pack presence to measure.
levers.gate: Owner decision; the owner verifies the profile personally. No agent creates, edits or verifies a profile.
levers.acceptance: Eligibility decision recorded with its reason; if a profile exists: verified, address hidden, name matches the website, categories and services describe only services actually delivered.

levers.action: Export a first GA4 and Search Console baseline, approve one keyword set and one grid, and pick a licensed rank tracker.
levers.rationale: Every target in MISSION_OBJECTIVES.json is relative to a baseline that does not exist yet.
levers.gate: Owner exports the data and approves collection and retention.
levers.acceptance: baseline_metrics.json sources move to 'collected' with evidence references; tools/exposure_contracts.py passes; a first run passes tools/geo_grid.py import.

levers.action: Use one business name everywhere: the live homepage structured data says 'ClearGlass Inc' while 82 other schema uses say 'ClearGlass Inc.'. Pick the real-world name and use it on the site, the Business Profile and every listing.
levers.rationale: Google asks that the profile name reflect the real-world name used consistently on the storefront, website and stationery.
levers.gate: Owner confirms the legal and trading name.

levers.action: Publish one business email on the company domain in structured data and contact sections instead of the personal iCloud address the live schema shows.
levers.rationale: A cyber-risk advisory listing a personal mailbox weakens trust; this checkout already uses an address on clearglassinc.com.
levers.gate: Owner decision and a working, authenticated mailbox on the domain.
levers.acceptance: One email across the site's structured data; nap-email-conflict findings are zero.

levers.action: Before this repository's rebuilt homepage is published anywhere, add the owner-confirmed locality (Burlington, ON) and service area to website/site_config.py, so the homepage keeps the Burlington signal the live homepage has today.
levers.rationale: The rebuilt index.html declares only the business name in its structured data and never mentions Burlington; the live homepage lists Burlington in areaServed and mentions it 6 times.
levers.gate: Owner supplies the real locality and service area; the website/README.md rule against invented values applies.
levers.acceptance: tools/local_seo_audit.py --root . lists the homepage under pages_with_locality_in_area_served, and tests/test_homepage.py passes.

levers.action: Carry the canonical fixes into the publishing repository. This repository fixed /procurement-legal-tech.html (it pointed to clearglassinc.github.io) and /smb.html on 2026-11-21, but the live pages still serve the old tags. Confirm that /apps/command-center/index.html -> /command-center.html is intended.
levers.rationale: A canonical on another host asks search engines to index that host's copy instead of the live page.
levers.gate: Site owner approves the change in the publishing repository.
levers.acceptance: canonical-mismatch findings are zero or each one is documented as intended.

levers.action: Turn the Burlington-targeted page into a real Burlington service page at a URL that says so, with Burlington in the H1, the services actually sold, real proof, and contact; keep /seo-authority-hub.html as an instant meta refresh redirect to it.
levers.rationale: Only one live page has Burlington in its title and its URL names an SEO tactic, not the service. GitHub Pages cannot send server-side redirects; Google treats an instant meta refresh as a permanent redirect.
levers.gate: Brand, legal and site-owner approval in the publishing repository.
levers.acceptance: No invented address, testimonial or case study; Burlington in the title and H1; valid structured data; no-local-landing-page finding cleared.

levers.action: After a Business Profile exists, ask every client with a completed engagement for an honest review, the same way, with no incentive.
levers.rationale: Google names review count as part of prominence, and prohibits selectively soliciting positive reviews or offering incentives.
levers.gate: Owner approves wording and sends; CASL basis recorded per recipient.
levers.acceptance: No NPS or sentiment filter decides who is asked; every request logged; opt-outs honoured within 10 business days.

levers.action: Propose one free workshop each to the Halton Region Small Business Centre and Burlington Public Library, then the Chamber.
levers.rationale: Verified local organizations whose audience is business owners; a workshop earns a genuine local listing and mention.
levers.gate: Owner approves each recipient and message; no automated follow-up.
levers.acceptance: Proposals logged with the official page they were based on; replies and opt-outs recorded.

levers.action: Publish two evidence-backed articles for Burlington and Halton business owners and link them to the Burlington page.
levers.rationale: Relevance comes from content that matches what local buyers search; volume without substance invites doorway and scaled-content problems.
levers.gate: Editor verifies sources, claims and rights before publication.
levers.acceptance: Each article has a distinct search intent, cited sources, a UTM-tagged call to action and a 30-day result.

levers.action: List the business on a few authoritative profiles (Business Profile, Bing Places, Apple Business Connect, Chamber directory if joined) with identical name, phone, website and service area.
levers.rationale: Consistency avoids confusing customers and search engines; bulk directory submission is excluded.
levers.gate: Owner approves the canonical record and each account change.
levers.acceptance: Before and after capture for each listing; no duplicates created.
